<!-- release-notes:start -->
## Release notes

### Highlights

- **Element IDs now name their database** — `elementId()` output gains the namespace segment, so the first node reads `4:relate-neo4j:n0` instead of `4:relate:n0` — in the shell, in JSON, and over Bolt; anything parsing element IDs will want the new shape. Example:
  ```
  relate --json "CREATE (n:Person) RETURN elementId(n)"
  ```

- **Shortest paths meet in the middle** — a `shortestPath` whose endpoints are property maps now seeks both ends and searches as a pair instead of balling out from one side, measured two orders of magnitude faster on hub-heavy graphs — and every traversal in the engine saves one read per hop besides. Example:
  ```
  relate -d ./friends "MATCH p = shortestPath((a:Person {name: 'Alice'})-[*..6]-(b:Person {name: 'Bob'})) RETURN p"
  ```

- **Cleanly-closed stores skip the reopen index rebuild** — when the WAL replays nothing, open no longer rebuilds the indexes, so a tidily shut-down store gets to its first row sooner. Example:
  ```
  relate query --database ./friends
  ```

### Other changes

- `relate upgrade` no longer prints the rename notice after its status line — just the facts, then the skill refresh.

<!-- release-notes:end -->
## What's Changed
* perf(storage): skip the post-replay index rebuild when the WAL replayed nothing (LABS-1112) by @jexp in https://github.com/relatedb/relate/pull/92
* test(research): land the per-structure heap-census harness by @jexp in https://github.com/relatedb/relate/pull/97
* chore(executor,front): bar() polish (LABS-1176) by @jexp in https://github.com/relatedb/relate/pull/103
* chore(eggs): egg polish — shared helpers, one Rng, panic payload (LABS-1182) by @jexp in https://github.com/relatedb/relate/pull/102
* ci(release): fold the retry re-stamp into the bump commit with --amend by @oskarhane in https://github.com/relatedb/relate/pull/106
* fix(core): make the element-id namespace segment dash-bearing (ADR-0554) by @jexp in https://github.com/relatedb/relate/pull/101
* feat(cli): drop the cypherlite rename notice from relate's upgrade by @oskarhane in https://github.com/relatedb/relate/pull/105
* perf(executor): shortest-path walk core and pair search for property-seekable endpoints (LABS-914, ADR-0556) by @jexp in https://github.com/relatedb/relate/pull/104


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/relatedb/relate/compare/v0.1.1...v0.1.2

<!-- release-notes:start -->
## Release notes

### Highlights

- **Wide-column Parquet snapshots** — `--snapshot-format` learns `parquet-wide`: the Parquet codec writes one typed column per promoted property key beside a residual tagged-JSON tail, and the next checkpoint pins the choice into the manifest so every later open keeps the store wide. Works on the query session and on `serve`.
  ```
  relate --snapshot-format parquet-wide ./friends
  ```

- **Full-text search learned Lucene manners** — fulltext `SEARCH` and the `db.index.fulltext.query*` procedures now pass the query syntax straight to the index (`AND`/`NOT` are operators, a lowercase `and` stays a term), rank hits with live BM25 pinned against Neo4j's own scores, page with `SKIP`/`OFFSET`, and evaluate `WITH ANALYZER` per row — English stemming included.
  ```
  relate ./movies "MATCH (m:Movie) SEARCH m IN (FULLTEXT INDEX moviePlots FOR 'princess AND NOT snow' LIMIT 5) RETURN m.title"
  ```

- **A quiet tune-up** — the engine got faster in three places you'll notice and none you'll have to think about:
  - POINT indexes moved to an R*-tree backend — radius and bounding-box seeks probe a packed tree instead of walking grid cells, antimeridian wrap included.
  - Label, relationship-type and property-key names resolve to token ids once per plan instead of hashing names per candidate.
  - `MATCH` predicates push to their earliest clause, and `UNWIND range()` streams into aggregating projections instead of piling up rows first.

### Other changes

- Java client: typed `QueryType`/`Namespace`/`Severity`/`Category` enums replace raw strings, and `PlanActual` carries the full wire plan shape.
- The variable-shadowing notification now looks inside `EXISTS`/`COUNT`/`COLLECT` expression subquery bodies.
- `SEARCH` over complex patterns (the `complex-search-patterns` preview) counts `LIMIT` survivors instead of pre-filter candidates.
- Scalar fixes: decimal `round()`, temporal sort order, nested-list type unions.
- Runtime lists now coerce to predicates at `WHERE`/`FILTER` positions.
- Duration fractions fold through Neo4j's approximate chain.
- `FINISH` is legal after a row-producing catalog command; DDL commands are standalone.
- The interactive REPL grew a hidden game cabinet — `.life`, `.snake`, `.tetris`, `.dash` (Archie runs, jumps and ducks) — and `.fortune` learned five new fortunes.

<!-- release-notes:end -->

<!-- release-notes:start -->
## Release notes

### Highlights

- **One binary, one file, nothing to deploy** — Relate is an embedded, in-memory property-graph engine that answers Cypher; a graph is a `.rl` file, a directory, or pure memory, and there is no server to babysit. Example:
  ```
  relate "RETURN 1 + 2 AS sum"
  ```

- **Durable by construction** — every committed write rides a fsync'd WAL, with Parquet checkpoints for fast reopens; `clone` packs a store into a single portable file for backup or transfer. Example:
  ```
  relate clone ./friends ./friends-backup.rl
  ```

- **One engine, every front door** — the same engine sits behind each of these, so a query that works in the shell works everywhere:
  - the `relate` CLI shell, interactive or one-shot
  - Python, Node.js, browser WASM, Rust, Java, Go, and Swift bindings over one typed C ABI
  - `relate serve` — one process speaking Bolt, the HTTP Query API v2, and MCP

### Other changes

- openCypher is the language contract: `MATCH`/`MERGE`, subqueries, schema DDL, 80+ built-in functions, quantified path patterns — the openCypher TCK is the measured dialect floor.
- Vector search: `vector()` properties, `vector.similarity.*` scoring, `CREATE VECTOR INDEX`, and the `SEARCH` clause for index-backed top-K.
- Geospatial: WGS-84 and Cartesian points, `point.distance()`, bounding-box predicates, and R-tree point indexes.
- `EXPLAIN` and `PROFILE` render the plan tree with per-operator rows and timing.
- `--read-only=live` lets a second process follow a store's WAL while another writes it.
- `pull` and `push` mirror subgraphs between Relate and a Neo4j/Aura instance over the Query API v2.
- `relate skill install` drops a skill bundle into detected AI agents so they drive the CLI correctly the first time.
- Userland extensions mount as `relate run <name>`; first-party packages import a filesystem tree or a git history as a graph.
- Anonymous usage metrics are on by default with a layered opt-out (`relate telemetry off`); query text and paths are structurally never collected.

<!-- release-notes:end -->
